title: Role assignment can record the wrong seat and then crash on duplicate provider names

finding.claim: Role assignment can record the wrong seat and then crash on duplicate provider names
finding.evidence: When a role spec builds to a seat name already present in `providers`, the code keeps the existing callable but still records the new role against that seat name. If the existing seat came from a different provider, later metadata generation indexes `providers[seat_name]` under the wrong assumptions and can fail or misattribute the role.
finding.recommendation: Detect collisions between an assigned role seat name and an existing provider seat built from a different spec. Either reject the configuration with a clear error, or namespace role-added seats so they cannot alias unrelated existing seats. Also derive role metadata from the actual callable inserted into `providers`, not just from `describe_spec(spec)`.

code_region.note: region text is the finding's validated evidence quote; full region could not be re-located at the record head

refutation.reason: The code explicitly records the seat name into seat_roles regardless of whether the seat already existed in providers. The assignment overwrites the mapping, meaning a role can alias an existing provider seat, and the recorded seat_roles entry reflects the new role assignment, not a collision reject
